title: KV granularity adaptation and scheduled defrag sweep for paged-attention
creator: Marco Li
description: Background: We observe sporadic decode tail latency spikes linked to high KV fragmentation and conservative allocation granularity when serving mixed-length traffic. Large numbers of small allocations increase bookkeeping overhead; large allocations increase internal fragmentation and reduce ability to reuse warmed fragments. Goal: implement a runtime policy that adapts KV allocation granularity per-tenant and workload hotset, and introduce a low-priority scheduled defragmentation sweep that consolidates free fragments during off-peak windows without impacting prefill throughput. Success criteria: 1) 10-25% reduction in 95th/99th decode latency tail attributable to KV stalls on canary tenants; 2) reduction in allocation churn (alloc+free ops) by 20% on mixed workloads; 3) no >1% increase in average token cost from background defrag CPU/DRAM overhead. Design overview: - Adaptive granularity: maintain per-tenant histogram of sequence-length and fragment reuse frequency (store as compact counters in runtime telemetry). Every N minutes evaluate whether to switch allocation bucket sizes (e.g., 256B, 512B, 1KB, 2KB logical slots) for that tenant's KV arena. Switching is incremental: new allocations use new bucket, old fragments can be compacted or left for reuse. - Defrag sweep: a background worker that runs during configurable low-priority windows (configurable per deployment: default 0200-0400 UTC for hosted). Sweep will coalesce adjacent free fragments into larger contiguous slots using lock-free handoffs where possible; when compaction requires copying live fragments, it will rate-limit itself by measuring prefill queue length and decode backlog. - Prefill interaction: Add a prefill admission threshold so prefill requests can be temporarily punted to fallback model variants if the defrag worker is active and decode latency SLOs are close to breach. - Eviction hints: When freeing fragments, annotate with age and reuse-score so the eviction policy prefers low-reuse, cold fragments first. Implementation plan: 1) telemetry prototype: add per-tenant histogram counters and fragment metadata fields (age, reuse_hits) to runtime logging. 2) allocation policy module: implement a background evaluator that outputs a tenant->bucket decision and a safe ramp plan. 3) defrag worker: implement sweep, copy-on-compact flow, and an admission limiter that reads runtime backlog signals. 4) integration: ensure prefill scheduler consults the defrag worker backpressure signal; add canary config knobs. Rollout: ; canary on 10 production tenants for 2 weeks; promote to 25% of traffic if metrics are favorable; global rollout if stable for 7 days. Metrics to monitor: decode_p95, decode_p99, kv_eviction_rate, kv_alloc_ops_per_min, fragment_utilization_ratio, background_compaction_cpu, prefill_retries, model-fallbacks. Risks and mitigations: - Defrag copying could contend with decode GPU transfers: mitigate by rate-limiting compaction during peak GPU utilization and prefer CPU-side copy to host memory first. - Incorrect bucket switching might regress tail latency for latency-sensitive tenants: mitigation via canary and gradual ramp with rollback thresholds. - Telemetry overhead: counters must be compact and sampled; start with per-minute aggregates. Open questions: - Optimal bucketing granularities given median sequence length distribution; propose offline simulation using historical traces. - Should tenants be allowed to pin a bucket for predictability? propose a tenant-level opt-out flag. Dependencies: requires compact telemetry primitives from ENG-61234 and eviction-policy hook from ENG-31807. Deliverables: design doc (confluence), telemetry PR, allocation policy PR, defrag worker PR, integration tests + load replay results. Estimated engineering effort: 5 points.
